answer.sameness: The set resolves into a few repeated families: white split heroes with bold sans-serif headings and rectangular photographs (atelje-bergant, kolesarski-servis-ovinek, steklarstvo-vrhovnik); framed cream cards, serif headings, leafy ornaments and arched photographs on dark backgrounds (sirarna-pr-simnu, urarstvo-tic); and landscape photographs with overlapping editorial cards (pivovarna-rov, vinarstvo-pinteric). Plesna-sola-takt adds an arch to the familiar split hero. Small wordmark headers, underlined secondary links, compact coloured buttons and image-first mobile stacks recur throughout. Burgundy, teal and forest green differentiate pages, but the underlying compositions remain conspicu­“
recurringIssues: Identical compositions and decorative details are reused across unrelated businesses, making parts of the portfolio look reskinned rather than individually designed.
Several desktop heroes leave substantial white space around small text blocks, weakening presence and making the layouts feel underdeveloped.
Mobile bottom action bars compete with page content and, on several screens, sit across photographs, cards or the beginning of the following section.
Many hero photographs show objects rather than people, premises or work in progress, giving the portfolio an impersonal, interchangeable promotional feel.
Tiny dark labels repeat across hero photographs and distract from otherwise clean presentations.
Optika-jasna's yellow, bracketed phone-number field looks like an unfinished implementation rather than a resolved form component.

best.why: The circular eyewear image, mint surround, coral arc and tilted information tag create the clearest distinctive visual identity, despite the unresolved-looking form.
The vineyard photograph and deep-green editorial panel establish a coherent atmosphere, with a particularly convincing image-to-content transition on mobile.
The expansive landscape, prominent masthead and inset cream card give this page a stronger sense of place and a more memorable composition than the standard split heroes.

weakest.why: The generic centred header, small copy block, disconnected glass photograph and large white gaps produce the least distinctive desktop composition.
A conventional split hero and broadly illustrative photograph underplay an architecture business, while the tall mobile contact header delays the main content.
Although visually tidy, its double-bordered card, leafy ornament and arched image duplicate the cheese page so closely that the watchmaker lacks an independent design language.

answer.oneChange: Require a genuinely different art-direction concept for each business before production, with its own hero structure, typographic hierarchy and photographic brief—not another palette applied to an existing composition.
answer.summary: This is a competent template portfolio, not yet a distinctive studio portfolio. Most pages are readable, the colour choices are controlled, and several mobile layouts hold together well. The weakness is repetition: unrelated businesses share not just components but entire visual concepts. The optics, brewery and winery pages show more character; the basic split heroes and duplicated ornamental cards pull the set back toward ordinary template work. Invest in business-specific art direction before adding more decorative variations, then tighten mobile action-bar behaviour and remove unfinished-looking interface details.
